projects.title: Deskmate
projects.description: Built backend logic and database storage for a workspace reservation application, helping offices manage a limited number of desks.

skills.usage: Implemented backend business logic and APIs.

skills.name: .NET
skills.usage: Built services and web endpoints using .NET.

projectImages.description: Deskmate application screenshot showing desk reservation interface.

caseStudy.problem: When a lot of people work remotely, you don't need too much space in the office, but if there's more people than desks, how will people know if there's space for them at any given time?
contributions: Worked on the backend logic for reserving seats.
Made sure the connection between backend and the database was done properly.
caseStudy.approach: By selecting a desk on the map you can reserve it for a time or see when it will be reserved by someone else. It was one large application with a MVC, BLL and DAL layer as it was what we were learning at the time.
caseStudy.result: Web application where you can see all desks, reserve one for yourself and don't have to worry about arriving to a full office any more.

projects.description: Researched API integrations and built backend logic for an AI-tool inventory application intended to support EU AI Act compliance work. Processed and stored information about the AI tools used by connected accounts.

skills.name: Google APIs
skills.usage: Got as much relevant data as possible from the API about AI tools used by an account.

skills.name: OpenAI APIs
skills.usage: Got as much relevant data as possible from the API about AI tools used by an account.

skills.usage: Sprint planning, retrospectives, and daily stand-ups.

skills.name: Team Coordination
skills.usage: Coordinated work between team members and our stakeholders.

projectImages.description: Here you can see details about a specific tool that you used.
CloudAIScanner overview where you see all the AI tools used by the currently logged in user.

caseStudy.problem: The EU AI Act was announced that would require all companies to clearly list the AI that they were using for any task at the company. For that a tool was needed to easily collect and list those.
caseStudy.approach: Using endpoints from Google and OpenAI, you can retrieve all API keys that are connected to your account/organisation. Then by filtering the results you get an overview of all the AI. After then confirming if that list is right you can submit it for review to the EU. As this project was done a year before the act went into effect most AI companies didn't have documentation or endpoints for this data yet, so we limited it to platforms that did have it.
caseStudy.result: A tool that allows users to list all used AIs/models that are in some way linked to connected accounts.

projects.title: Smart Classroom
projects.description: Developed a 'Smart Classroom' where people can track assets moving around classrooms and track the air quality. I worked on receiving the data from the gateway devices, storing it and displaying it in a web application.

skills.name: IoT
skills.usage: We used Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) for device communication.

skills.name: MongoDB
skills.usage: All the sensor data was stored in MongoDB.

skills.name: TypeScript
skills.usage: We used TypeScript for type-safe code.

skills.name: Problem Solving
skills.usage: Hardware & software troubleshooting. This was necessary for integrating various components since there was not a lot of documentation.

skills.name: Team Coordination
skills.usage: Collaborated with hardware and software teams from different semesters to combine our knowledge and experience.

projectVideo.description: Feature walkthrough: asset tracking in real time; air-quality sensing with a Thingy:52; live movement of sensors on the map; an inventory-style device list; editing device names; sorting the list; choosing which columns to show; adding a new device; reading the legend; and filtering by device type.

projectImages.description: Smart Classroom screenshot from the demo video showing the dashboard with all the sensors, beacons and tags.

caseStudy.problem: Technology and IoT are often portrayed with robots at Fontys Open Days. But there's so much more to it. So how about showing what it could do within a classroom?
contributions: Worked on the backend logic and data storage.
caseStudy.approach: By having sensors continuously send data to the backend, you can track all sorts of things about a classroom such as the air quality. And using triangulation with beacons, you can even track the approximate location of a bluetooth tag in rooms.
caseStudy.result: A fun showcase to show students what other applications of the subjects Technology and IoT are possible at Fontys.

projects.title: Yookr Monitoring Tool
projects.description: Designed and developed a service-monitoring prototype during my internship. Combined service logs, warnings, errors, and performance metrics in a dashboard to help the team understand application health.

skills.name: Docker
skills.usage: Containerized services. The logs were also gotten from there.

projectImages.description: This image shows the health and current status of the monitored services. This was colour coded based on warning and error logs, with black being fully down.
Here you can see the page that tracked performance metrics for each environment and service.

caseStudy.problem: Yookr had a lot of applications it was developing and testing but barely any way to monitor them. This created a lot of time loss when anything went wrong.
contributions: Created a tool that shows the current status of applications, shows error logs and current performance metrics.
caseStudy.approach: All applications were put in docker containers. Using the bollard crate, the application got all information that the developers wanted and showed them on a webpage. I then set up a Raspberry Pi to have the site open at all times so we could show the main screen on a monitor within the office and immediately see if an application was experiencing a problem.
caseStudy.result: It was adopted immediately, though not long after we switched to Kubernetes and on that using Prometheus and Grafana we replaced my application.

projectImages.description: Game Analysis - Detailed statistics and progress for games that I have played
Games Library - Collection of my favourite games and games that I am currently playing
Music Collection - Collection of my favourite music

caseStudy.problem: People often ask me for my favourite shows, movies, music or games. But quite often I just can't think of the ones I want to say or they don't know what I'm talking about.
contributions: Connected relevant API for all categories and made sure to comply with their terms of service.
Created data analysis based on received data.
caseStudy.approach:
In my own admin panel, I can add favourites for every category using the external API listed on the relevant page. From there I save them in a database with link to the original API so not every page visit requires a call to the external API.

For game analysis. When using Steam's API, you can get a lot of data about the user's games, some of those include the genres, time spend playing and achievement completion percentage. Based on that I created some fun stats that I wanted to see for myself but also explains a lot about me as a person (Such as my love for Hack&Slash, RPG and Strategy games).
caseStudy.result: Nice and easy overview site that I can show people to have them instantly get a feeling on who I am as a person.
